To help you fix the MMS (picture messaging) issue, I’ll need to ask a few questions and guide you through some quick checks on your phone. Are you able to make regular calls and use mobile data (for example, browsing the web) on your phone right now? This will help determine if the issue is specific to MMS or related to your overall service.

I’m not sure about making calls or using the internet right now—my phone says there’s no service, and I can’t send picture messages at all. Does that mean something’s wrong with my service? What should I do next?

Thank you for the information. Your line ending in 2002 is currently active, so there shouldn’t be a suspension or billing issue affecting your service.

Since your phone says “no service,” let’s try to restore your cellular connection. Please follow these steps on your phone:
1. Check if Airplane Mode is turned ON. If it is, turn it OFF.
2. If Airplane Mode is already OFF, try restarting your phone.

After doing this, let me know if your phone still says “no service.” If it does, I’ll guide you through the next troubleshooting steps.

Okay, I just turned Airplane Mode off. Now I see a little signal bar at the top, and it says "2G" with something about data being enabled. Is that good? Should I try sending a picture message again, or is there something else I need to do?

Thank you for the update! Seeing a signal bar and “2G” means your phone is now connected to the network, but 2G is generally not suitable for sending picture messages (MMS). MMS usually requires at least a 3G, 4G, or 5G connection.

Let’s improve your network connection:
1. Please go to your phone’s network settings.
2. Change your network mode to “4G/5G preferred” (or similar wording).

Once you’ve done this, check if your phone connects to 3G, 4G, or 5G. Let me know what you see, and then we can try sending a picture message again. If you need help finding the network mode setting, let me know your phone model and I can guide you.

Alright, I changed the network mode like you said. Now the top of my screen shows a strong signal and says "5G." Is that what we want? Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there something else I need to do first?

That’s perfect! Now that your phone is connected to 5G with a strong signal, please try sending a picture message (MMS) again.

Let me know if it goes through successfully or if you still experience any issues. If it doesn’t work, I’ll guide you through the next troubleshooting steps.
I just tried sending a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. It’s a bit frustrating—everything looks fine with the signal now, but the message just won’t send. What should I do next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your signal is strong and you’re on 5G, let’s check a few more things that can affect MMS:

1. Is your mobile data turned ON (not just Wi-Fi)?
2. Are you connected to a Wi-Fi network, or just using mobile data?
3. Do you see any error messages when trying to send the picture message?

Please let me know your answers, and I’ll guide you through the next steps to resolve this.

My mobile data is turned on, and I’m not connected to Wi-Fi—just using mobile data. When I try to send a picture message, it just doesn’t go through, but I don’t see any specific error message. What should I try next?

Thank you for confirming that mobile data is ON and you’re not connected to Wi-Fi. The next common cause for MMS issues is incorrect APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for picture messaging to work.

Let’s try resetting your APN settings to default. Here’s what to do:
1. Go to your phone’s network or cellular settings.
2. Find the “Access Point Names” or “APN” section.
3. Select the option to “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.”

After resetting the APN settings, please restart (reboot) your phone. Once your phone is back on, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if you need step-by-step instructions for your specific phone model, or if you have any trouble finding these settings.

I’ve reset the APN settings like you said. But I’m a little nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Can you reassure me before I go ahead and reboot?

Restarting (rebooting) your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or personal data. It simply turns your phone off and back on, refreshing its system and network connections. All your files, apps, and settings will remain unchanged.

It’s safe to proceed with the restart. Once your phone is back on, please try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works.
Okay, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s really starting to worry me—why isn’t this working? Is there anything else we can try?

Thank you for your patience. Since you’ve reset your APN settings, restarted your phone, have a strong 5G signal, and mobile data is on, let’s check a few more possible causes:

1. Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS. Could you check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your phone? If it is, please turn it OFF and try sending a picture message again.
2. The messaging app needs permission to access storage and SMS. If you know how, please check your messaging app’s permissions and make sure it has access to both storage and SMS.

Please let me know if you need help with these steps, or if you try them and the issue still isn’t resolved.

I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. My messaging app also has permission for storage and SMS. Is there anything else that could be causing this? I’m really hoping we can get this fixed soon.

Hi there. I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called?—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and they just won’t go through. Can you help me fix this?

To assist you with your MMS (picture messaging) issue, I’ll need to verify your account first. Could you please provide one of the following:
- Your phone number,
- Your customer ID,
- Or your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format)?

Once I have this information, I can begin troubleshooting the problem for you.

Thank you for providing your phone number. I’m ready to help you troubleshoot your MMS (picture messaging) issue.

To get started, could you please let me know:
- Are you able to make regular calls and send/receive standard text messages (SMS) without any issues?
- Are you currently connected to mobile data (not just Wi-Fi)?

This information will help me narrow down the cause and guide you through the right steps.
I can still make regular calls and send normal text messages without any trouble. Right now, I’m not connected to Wi-Fi—just using my mobile data, and it looks like that’s turned on.

Thank you for the details. Since you can make calls and send texts, and your mobile data appears to be on, let’s check a few technical settings that can affect MMS.

Could you please check if you can send MMS from your messaging app? If you’re not sure how, I can guide you through a quick check. Would you like to proceed with that?
I just checked, and it seems like my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking. The next step is to verify your phone’s network connection and settings, as MMS requires at least a 3G/4G/5G connection and correct configuration.

Could you please check and let me know what type of network your phone is currently connected to (e.g., 2G, 3G, 4G, 5G)? If you’re unsure how to check this, I can guide you through the process. Would you like instructions?
Oh, I’m not really sure how to check what kind of network I’m on. Could you please walk me through it? I get a bit lost with these things.

No problem! I can guide you through checking your network type. Here’s what you can do:

1. Look at the top of your phone’s screen (the status bar). You should see some icons near the signal bars.
2. Look for a label like “5G,” “4G,” “LTE,” “3G,” or “E.” This indicates your current network type.
3. If you don’t see any of those, let me know what icons or words you do see near your signal bars.

If you’re still unsure, just describe what you see in the status bar, and I’ll help you interpret it!
At the top of my screen, I see something that says “5G” next to the signal bars. Does that mean I’m on the right kind of network?

Yes, seeing “5G” next to your signal bars means you are connected to a suitable network for sending MMS. Since your network connection is good, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN settings are a common cause of MMS issues.

Would you like instructions on how to check your APN settings, or would you prefer to reset them to default to ensure they’re correct? Resetting is often the quickest fix and is safe to do.

I’m not really sure what APN settings are, and I get nervous messing with things I don’t understand. If resetting them is safe and won’t mess up my photos or anything important, maybe we could try that? Will it change anything else on my phone?

Resetting your APN settings is safe and will not affect your photos, messages, or any personal data on your phone. It only restores the network settings your phone uses to connect to your carrier for mobile data and MMS. This often resolves issues with sending picture messages.

After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect. Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings, or do you want me to guide you through the process interactively?

Alright, I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. You mentioned I’ll need to restart my phone now—will that erase anything, like my photos or messages? I just want to be sure before I do it.

Restarting your phone will not erase any of your photos, messages, or personal data. It simply turns your phone off and back on, which helps apply the new network settings.

You can safely restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try sending an MMS (picture message) again to see if the issue is resolved. If you still have trouble, let me know and we’ll continue troubleshooting together.
Okay, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—this is all a bit much for me.

Thank you for your patience, and I understand this can be frustrating. Let’s try a couple more quick checks that often resolve MMS issues:

1. Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS. Could you check if Wi-Fi Calling is turned on? If you’re not sure how, I can guide you through checking and turning it off if needed.
2. Also, your messaging app needs permission to access storage and SMS. Would you like help checking if your messaging app has the right permissions?

Please let me know which step you’d like to try first, or if you’d like me to walk you through both. I’m here to help you every step of the way.
I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned on. Should I turn that off? Will that mess up anything else on my phone? I just want to make sure it’s safe before I do anything.

Turning off Wi-Fi Calling is safe and will not affect your photos, messages, or any other data on your phone. It simply means your phone will use the regular cellular network for calls and texts instead of Wi-Fi. This can help fix MMS issues, especially if your carrier doesn’t support MMS over Wi-Fi.

You can go ahead and turn off Wi-Fi Calling. After that, try sending a picture message again. If it still doesn’t work, let me know and we’ll continue troubleshooting together.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really hoping we can get this working soon.

Thank you for letting me know. Let’s check one more important setting: your messaging app’s permissions. The app needs permission to access storage and SMS to send picture messages.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to check and update your messaging app’s permissions? If you’re not sure how to do this, I can guide you through it. Just let me know!
I checked, and it looks like my messaging app already has permission for storage and phone. Is that enough, or does it need something else to send picture messages?

Your messaging app should also have permission for SMS (text messaging) in addition to storage. This is necessary for sending and receiving both regular and picture messages.

Could you please check if the SMS permission is enabled for your messaging app? If it’s not, enable it and then try sending a picture message again. If you need help finding this setting, let me know your phone type (Android or iPhone), and I can provide step-by-step instructions.
I went ahead and gave the messaging app permission for SMS, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to worry this will never work.

Hi there. My phone has been saying "No Service" for a few hours now, and I’m not sure what to do. I just want to be able to make calls again. Can you help me, please?

To assist you with the "No Service" issue and help you make calls again, I need to identify your account and phone line. Could you please provide me with your phone number or your full name along with your date of birth for verification?
My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

{"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}

{"line_id": "L1001", "phone_number": "555-123-2001", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1001", "device_id": "D1001", "data_used_gb": 3.2, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2025-01-10", "last_sim_replacement_date": null, "suspension_start_date": null}

{"line_id": "L1003", "phone_number": "555-123-2003", "status": "Suspended", "plan_id": "P1001", "device_id": "D1003", "data_used_gb": 0.0, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-06-30", "last_plan_change_date": "2024-10-05", "last_sim_replacement_date": null, "suspension_start_date": "2025-02-01"}

I found your account and the phone lines associated with it. The phone number you provided (555-123-2002) is active and not suspended. To diagnose the "No Service" issue, I will need to check the status of your phone's cellular service and SIM card. May I proceed with checking the status on your phone?
Yes, please go ahead and check whatever you need. I just want to get this fixed.
Please provide me with the type of your device or the operating system (e.g., iPhone, Android) so I can guide you through the necessary diagnostic checks on your phone.
I’m not sure about the type of phone, but I do see a little airplane icon at the top of my screen. Does that help?

Yes, the airplane icon indicates that Airplane Mode might be enabled on your phone, which disables all wireless communications including cellular service. This could be the reason for the "No Service" message.

I will guide you to check and turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. Please confirm if you want me to proceed with instructions to disable Airplane Mode.
Yes, please tell me how to turn it off. I didn’t even know I had that on!

To turn off Airplane Mode on your phone, please follow these general steps:

1. Swipe down from the top of your phone's screen to open the quick settings menu (or swipe up from the bottom on some phones).
2. Look for the airplane icon (✈️) in the quick settings.
3. If the airplane icon is highlighted or colored, it means Airplane Mode is ON.
4. Tap the airplane icon once to turn Airplane Mode OFF.
5. Wait a few moments for your phone to reconnect to the cellular network.

After turning off Airplane Mode, check if your phone shows signal bars and if you can make calls. If you still have issues, please let me know.
Okay, I turned off the airplane thing like you said. But now, at the top, it says "No Signal" and I still can’t make any calls. What should I do next?

Next, let's check the status of your SIM card to ensure it is properly recognized and active on your phone. This can help us determine if the SIM card is causing the "No Signal" issue.

Please confirm if you want me to guide you through checking the SIM card status on your phone.
Oh, it looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. What does that mean? Is that bad?

If your phone says there is no SIM card detected, it means your phone is not recognizing the SIM card physically inserted in the device. This is likely why you have "No Signal" and cannot make calls.

This can happen if the SIM card is not properly seated or inserted, or if there is an issue with the SIM card itself.

I recommend you try to reseat the SIM card by removing it and reinserting it carefully. If you want, I can guide you through the steps to reseat the SIM card. Would you like me to do that?
I get a bit nervous with things like that—will I lose any of my photos or anything if I take the SIM card out and put it back in?

No, removing and reinserting the SIM card will not cause you to lose any photos, apps, or personal data stored on your phone. The SIM card mainly stores your phone number and carrier information, not your personal files.

If you feel comfortable, I can guide you step-by-step through the process of reseating the SIM card to help resolve the issue. Would you like me to proceed with that?
Alright, I went ahead and took out the SIM card and put it back in, just like you said. But it still says "No Signal" at the top. Is there anything else we can try? This is getting a bit frustrating.

I understand the frustration. Let's continue troubleshooting to get your service back.

Next, I will guide you to check your phone's network status and settings to identify any other possible causes of the "No Signal" issue.

May I proceed with checking your phone's network status and related settings?
It looks like my SIM card is now saying something about being "locked_pin." I’m not sure what that means. Is that why I still have no service?

Yes, if your SIM card is showing as "locked_pin," it means the SIM card is locked with a PIN code. This lock prevents the phone from accessing the cellular network until the correct PIN is entered. This is likely the reason you still have no service.

Unfortunately, unlocking a SIM card with a PIN requires you to enter the correct PIN code on your phone. If you enter the wrong PIN multiple times, the SIM may become locked with a PUK code, which is more complicated to resolve.

Since this involves security and PIN code entry on your device, I cannot unlock the SIM for you remotely. You will need to enter the correct PIN on your phone to unlock the SIM.

If you do not know the PIN or have forgotten it, you may need to contact your carrier or check your SIM card documentation for the default PIN or PUK code.

If you want, I can transfer you to a human agent for further assistance with SIM security issues. Would you like me to do that?
Oh, I see. I don’t remember ever setting a PIN for my SIM card. Is there a way to find out what it is, or should I just try a few numbers? I’m worried about making it worse.

It's important not to try random PIN numbers because entering the wrong PIN multiple times will lock your SIM card with a PUK code, which is more difficult to resolve.

Typically, the default SIM PIN is provided by your carrier and may be found in the documentation that came with your SIM card or on the carrier's website.

Since this is a security-related issue with your SIM card, and I cannot access or reset your SIM PIN remotely, I recommend contacting your carrier's customer support or visiting a store for assistance with unlocking your SIM card safely.

If you want, I can transfer you to a human agent who may be able to assist you further with this issue. Would you like me to do that?
Yes, I think it’s best if I talk to a real person about this. Could you please transfer me to someone who can help with the SIM card PIN? Thank you for your patience.

Hi there. My phone has been saying "No Service" for a few hours now, and I’m not sure what to do. I just want to be able to make calls and get messages again. Can you help me, please?

I can help you with that. To assist you better, could you please provide me with the phone number associated with your account or the phone number of the line that is showing "No Service"? This will allow me to check your account and line status.
Oh, sure. My phone number is 555-123-2002.

{"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}

{"line_id": "L1001", "phone_number": "555-123-2001", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1001", "device_id": "D1001", "data_used_gb": 3.2, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2025-01-10", "last_sim_replacement_date": null, "suspension_start_date": null}

{"line_id": "L1002", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1002", "device_id": "D1002", "data_used_gb": 8.7, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": true, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2024-12-15", "last_sim_replacement_date": "2025-01-20", "suspension_start_date": null}

Your line with phone number 555-123-2002 is currently active and not suspended. To help diagnose the "No Service" issue, I will need to check some technical details on your phone such as the status bar, SIM card status, and network status. May I proceed with guiding you through some diagnostic checks on your phone?
Yes, that’s fine. I’m not very good with technical things though, so please go slow and explain everything simply. What do you need me to do first?

Thank you for letting me know. Let's start with a simple check of your phone's status bar to see what it is currently showing regarding your network connection.

Please perform the check_status_bar action on your phone and tell me what icons or messages you see at the top of your screen. This will help us understand if your phone is detecting any network signal or if there are any special modes enabled like Airplane Mode.
At the top of my screen, I see an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any bars for signal or anything else about the network. What does the airplane mean?

The airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is currently turned ON on your phone. When Airplane Mode is on, it disables all wireless communications including cellular service, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth. This is why you are seeing "No Service" and no signal bars.

To restore your cellular service and be able to make calls and get messages, you need to turn OFF Airplane Mode on your phone.

Please go to your phone's settings or quick access menu and turn OFF Airplane Mode. Let me know once you have done that, and we will continue troubleshooting if needed.

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now, at the top of my screen, I see something that looks like a circle with a line through it and it says "No Signal." There’s also something about data being disabled. What should I do next?

Thank you for turning off Airplane Mode. The "No Signal" icon means your phone is not detecting any cellular network signal, and the data being disabled means mobile data is currently turned off.

Let's check the SIM card status next to make sure your SIM card is working properly. This will help us understand if the SIM card might be causing the issue.

Please perform the check_sim_status action on your phone and tell me what it shows about the SIM card status.
It says there’s no SIM card detected in the phone. Does that mean something is wrong with my SIM card? I haven’t touched it or anything.

If your phone says there is no SIM card detected, it usually means the phone is not recognizing the SIM card. This could be due to the SIM card being improperly seated or a temporary connection issue.

The next step is to try reseating the SIM card. This means removing the SIM card from your phone and then reinserting it carefully to ensure it is properly placed.

Please power off your phone, remove the SIM card, wait a few seconds, then reinsert the SIM card securely, and power your phone back on. Let me know once you have done this.
Oh, I get really nervous about taking things out of my phone. Will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do this? And do I really have to turn the phone off first?

I understand your concern. Removing and reinserting the SIM card will not delete any of your photos, messages, or personal data stored on your phone. The SIM card mainly stores your phone number and network information, not your personal files.

It is recommended to turn off your phone before removing the SIM card to avoid any potential damage to the SIM card or phone hardware. This is a precaution to keep everything safe.

If you feel uncomfortable doing this yourself, I can assist you with other troubleshooting steps or help you get in touch with a human agent for further assistance. What would you prefer?

Alright, I went ahead and did what you said—I turned off the phone, took out the SIM card, put it back in, and turned the phone on again. But it still says "No Signal" at the top, and data is still disabled. Is there something else I can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried.

Thank you for trying that. Since the SIM card is still not being recognized properly, let's check the network status on your phone to gather more information about the connection and data settings.

Please perform the check_network_status action on your phone and tell me what it shows regarding:
- Airplane Mode status
- Signal strength
- Network type (e.g., 5G, 4G)
- Mobile data status (enabled or disabled)
- Data roaming status (enabled or disabled)

This will help us understand the current network conditions better.

Okay, here’s what it shows:

- Airplane Mode is off.
- It says the SIM card status is "locked_pin."
- Cellular connection says "no service" and there’s no signal.
- Network type says "none."
- Mobile data is enabled.
- Data roaming is not enabled.
- Wi-Fi is off and not connected.

What does "locked_pin" mean for the SIM card?

The "locked_pin" status means that your SIM card is locked with a PIN code. This usually happens if the SIM card requires you to enter a PIN code to unlock it before it can connect to the network. Until the correct PIN is entered, the SIM card will not be active, and you will see "No Service."

To resolve this, you need to enter the SIM PIN code on your phone. Usually, the default SIM PIN is provided by your carrier or is printed on the SIM card packaging. If you don't know the PIN or enter it incorrectly multiple times, the SIM card may become locked and require a PUK code to unlock.

Please check if your phone is prompting you to enter the SIM PIN. If so, enter the correct PIN to unlock the SIM card. If you are unsure of the PIN or need help with this, let me know.

Oh, I see. I do remember seeing something pop up about a PIN, but I didn’t know what it was for, so I just ignored it. I’m not sure what my SIM PIN is—where would I find that? And what happens if I get it wrong? I really don’t want to mess anything up.

Your SIM PIN is a security code set by your carrier to protect your SIM card from unauthorized use. If you don't know your SIM PIN, it is often the default code provided by your carrier when you first got the SIM card. Common default PINs are "0000" or "1234," but it can vary.

If you enter the wrong SIM PIN multiple times (usually three attempts), your SIM card will become locked, and you will need a PUK (Personal Unblocking Key) code to unlock it. The PUK code is also provided by your carrier and is usually found in your SIM card documentation or by contacting customer support.

To avoid locking your SIM card, please try to find the correct SIM PIN from your carrier's documentation or contact them directly for assistance. If you want, I can help you get in touch with a human agent for further help with SIM PIN or PUK issues. Would you like me to do that?

I’m not sure where my SIM card paperwork is, and I really don’t want to risk locking it up. Maybe it’s best if I talk to a real person who can walk me through this? Could you please connect me to someone who can help with the PIN or PUK code?

Please confirm if you are able to perform diagnostic checks on your phone, so I can guide you through the necessary steps.
It looks like my phone isn’t detecting the SIM card—it says there’s no SIM card inserted. What should I do to fix this?

If your phone is showing that there is no SIM card inserted, the SIM card might be improperly seated or there could be a connection issue.

Please try the following:
1. Power off your phone.
2. Remove the SIM card from its slot.
3. Carefully reinsert the SIM card, ensuring it is properly seated.
4. Power your phone back on.

Let me know once you have done this, and I will guide you through the next steps.

I’ve removed and reinserted the SIM card as you instructed, but my phone is still showing “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” in the status bar. Is there anything else I should try? It’s getting a bit frustrating.

Your device "Smartphone Pro Max" is activated and associated with your active line. Since reinserting the SIM card did not resolve the issue and your phone still shows "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," the problem might be related to the SIM card or device configuration.

Since the SIM card is properly seated and the line is active, the next step is to check your phone's network status and settings to identify any configuration issues that might be causing the "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" problem.

Please confirm if you can perform diagnostic checks on your phone, so I can guide you through checking the network status and other relevant settings.
I checked the network status, and it says the SIM card is locked with a PIN. Could this be causing the “No Service” issue? What should I do to unlock it?

Yes, if your SIM card is locked with a PIN, it will prevent your phone from connecting to the network, causing the "No Service" issue.

To resolve this, you need to enter the correct SIM PIN on your phone to unlock it. If you enter the wrong PIN multiple times, the SIM may become locked and require a PUK code to unlock.

Please enter your SIM PIN on your phone to unlock it. If you do not know the PIN or have forgotten it, you may need to contact your carrier or check your SIM card documentation for the default PIN or PUK code.

If you need further assistance after unlocking the SIM, please let me know.
Thank you for explaining! I’ll try entering my SIM PIN now. If I have any trouble or if the issue isn’t resolved after unlocking, I’ll let you know.
You're welcome! Take your time entering the SIM PIN. If you encounter any issues or if the problem persists after unlocking, feel free to reach out, and I'll be here to assist you further.
I’ve entered my SIM PIN, but the status bar is still showing “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” Is there anything else I should try?

Since your SIM card is unlocked but you still see "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," let's proceed with checking your phone's network mode preference to ensure it is set to a mode that supports good connectivity.

May I guide you through checking and setting your network mode preference to 4G/5G preferred?
I checked, and my network mode preference is already set to “4G/5G preferred.” What should I try next?

Since your network mode preference is already set to "4G/5G preferred," the next step is to check if your mobile data is enabled on your phone and if there are any data restrictions or data saver modes active that might be disabling data.

Would you like me to guide you through checking and enabling mobile data and disabling any data restrictions on your phone?
I’ve turned mobile data on, and data saver mode is off, but the status bar still shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” What else can I try?

Since mobile data is on and data saver mode is off, but you still see "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," let's check if your phone has airplane mode enabled, which would disable all wireless connections.

Would you like me to guide you through checking and disabling airplane mode on your phone?
I checked, and airplane mode is already off. The SIM card status still says “locked_pin,” even though I entered my PIN earlier. Is there something else I should do to unlock it?

If your SIM card status still shows "locked_pin" after entering your PIN, it means the SIM card is still locked and the PIN entry may not have been accepted or processed correctly by the phone.

Please try the following:
1. Restart your phone and enter the SIM PIN again when prompted.
2. If the SIM remains locked, double-check that you are entering the correct PIN.
3. If you have entered the wrong PIN multiple times, your SIM may be blocked and require a PUK code to unlock.

If you do not have the PUK code or are unsure, you will need to contact your carrier's customer support to obtain the PUK code and unlock your SIM.

If you want, I can transfer you to a human agent for further assistance with SIM unlocking. Would you like me to do that?

Let me try restarting my phone and entering the SIM PIN again. If it still doesn’t work, I might need help with the PUK code or to speak with a human agent. I’ll let you know what happens after I try this.

That sounds like a good plan. Please try restarting your phone and entering the SIM PIN again. If you still face issues or need help with the PUK code or speaking to a human agent, just let me know. I'm here to assist you whenever you need.
I restarted my phone and entered the SIM PIN again, but I’m still seeing “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” in the status bar. What should I do next?

prompt.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi, I’m having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing is going through. Can you help me fix this?

To assist you with the MMS sending issue, I need to identify your account and phone line. Could you please provide me with your phone number or your full name along with your date of birth for verification?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else for verification.

To troubleshoot the MMS sending issue, I will need to check the status of your phone's cellular service, mobile data, and MMS capabilities. Let's start by checking the status bar on your phone to see the current network and data status. May I proceed with that?
Yes, please go ahead and check the status bar. Let me know what you find or if you need anything from my side.

I have confirmed your line is active and not suspended. Now, to proceed with the troubleshooting, I need to check the status bar on your phone to see the current network and data status. Could you please run the "check_status_bar" diagnostic action on your phone and tell me what icons or messages you see in the status bar at the top of your screen?
In my status bar, I see a poor signal icon, it says 2G, mobile data is enabled, and my battery is at 80%. What should I do next?

The status bar shows you have a poor signal and are connected to a 2G network. MMS requires at least a 3G network to work properly, so being on 2G could be the cause of your MMS sending issue.

I recommend changing your phone's network mode preference to allow 4G and 5G connections, which should improve your network quality and enable MMS functionality.

May I proceed to set your network mode preference to "4g_5g_preferred"?
Yes, please go ahead and set my network mode preference to "4g_5g_preferred." Let me know once it’s done or if you need anything else from me.

I am ready to proceed with setting your network mode preference to "4g_5g_preferred." However, this action requires interaction with your phone device to change the network mode preference. 

Please perform the following on your phone:
- Go to your phone's network settings.
- Find the option for "Network Mode" or "Preferred Network Type."
- Change it to "4G/5G Preferred" or a similar option that includes 4G and 5G.

After you do this, please reboot your phone and then try sending an MMS message again. Let me know if you need further assistance or if the issue persists.

I’ve changed the network mode to “4G/5G Preferred” as you suggested. I’ll go ahead and reboot my phone now. Once it’s back on, should I try sending an MMS right away, or do you want me to check anything else first?

After rebooting your phone, please try sending an MMS message right away. This will help us determine if changing the network mode resolved the issue.

If the MMS still does not send, please let me know, and we can proceed with further troubleshooting steps such as checking your APN settings, Wi-Fi Calling status, and messaging app permissions.
I rebooted my phone and tried sending an MMS, but it still won’t go through. The issue is still there—what should I try next?

Next, let's check the APN settings on your phone to ensure they are correct, especially the MMSC URL, which is crucial for MMS to work.

Please run the "check_apn_settings" diagnostic action on your phone and tell me what the current APN name and MMSC URL are. This will help us determine if the APN settings might be causing the MMS issue.
My current APN name is set to "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." Do these settings look correct, or should I change anything?

Your APN name and MMSC URL appear to be set, which is good. However, sometimes the APN settings can still be incorrect or corrupted even if they look right.

To ensure the APN settings are fully correct, I recommend resetting your APN settings to the default carrier settings. After resetting, you will need to reboot your phone for the changes to take effect.

May I guide you through resetting your APN settings now?
Yes, please guide me through resetting the APN settings. I’m ready to follow your instructions.

To reset your APN settings to the default carrier settings, please follow these steps on your phone:

1. Open the Settings app.
2. Go to "Network & Internet" or "Connections" (the exact name may vary by phone model).
3. Tap on "Mobile Network" or "Cellular Network."
4. Find and tap on "Access Point Names" or "APN."
5. Look for an option to "Reset to default" or "Reset APN" and select it.
6. Confirm the reset if prompted.

After you have reset the APN settings, please reboot your phone to apply the changes.

Once your phone has restarted, try sending an MMS message again and let me know if it works or if you need further assistance.
I followed your instructions to reset the APN settings and rebooted my phone, but I still can’t send MMS messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—what else can we try?

Let's continue troubleshooting your MMS issue by checking a few more things that could affect MMS functionality:

1. Wi-Fi Calling: Sometimes Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS. Could you please check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your phone? If it is, try turning it off.

2. Messaging App Permissions: The messaging app needs permissions to access storage and SMS to send MMS. Please check if the messaging app has these permissions granted.

Please let me know the status of Wi-Fi Calling and if you need help checking or changing app permissions.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned off on my phone, and my messaging app already has permissions for SMS, storage, and phone. What should I try next?

Your line is active, on a Premium Plan with a 15GB data limit, and you have used 8.7GB of data this cycle, so your data plan is not exceeded.

Since your Wi-Fi Calling is off and your messaging app has the necessary permissions, and your APN settings are correct, the MMS issue is not due to these common causes.

At this point, I recommend checking the mobile data connection quality and speed on your phone to ensure it is sufficient for MMS.

Please run the "run_speed_test" diagnostic action on your phone and tell me the result (e.g., download speed quality). This will help us determine if the mobile data connection is causing the MMS problem.
I tried running a speed test, but it failed and said "No Connection." Does this mean there’s an issue with my mobile data connection? What should I do next?

Yes, a "No Connection" result on the speed test indicates that your mobile data connection is not working properly, which would prevent MMS from sending.

Let's troubleshoot your mobile data connection:

1. Please check if Airplane Mode is ON on your phone. If it is, turn it OFF.
2. Ensure mobile data is enabled on your phone.
3. Since your line is not roaming enabled, if you are traveling outside your home network, mobile data will not work. Please confirm if you are currently traveling outside your carrier's coverage area.

Please check these and let me know what you find. If needed, I can guide you through the steps to toggle these settings.

Airplane Mode is off, mobile data is enabled, and I’m currently connected to a 2G network with poor signal. Data roaming is not enabled, and I am traveling outside my home country (I’m in France right now). Could this be the reason my mobile data and MMS aren’t working?

Yes, since you are traveling outside your home country and your line is not roaming enabled, your mobile data connection will not work, which also prevents MMS from working.

I can enable international data roaming on your line at no cost to you. This will allow you to use mobile data and send MMS messages while you are in France.

May I proceed to enable roaming on your line?

Yes, please go ahead and enable international data roaming on my line. I’d like to be able to use mobile data and send MMS while I’m here. Let me know once it’s done or if I need to do anything on my phone.

Hi, I’m having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone. It’s been happening for the past few hours, and I’d like to get it fixed so I can send pictures again. Can you help me with this?
To assist you with the MMS issue, I need to identify your account first. Could you please provide me with your phone number or your full name along with your date of birth for verification?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need any more information to verify my account.

I have identified your account and the phone line you are using. To troubleshoot the MMS sending issue, I will need to check the status of your phone's cellular service, mobile data, and MMS capabilities. May I proceed with running diagnostic checks on your phone?
Yes, please go ahead and run the diagnostic checks. Let me know what you find or if you need anything from my side.
I will start by checking the status bar, network status, SIM status, APN settings, and MMS sending capability on your phone.

I have confirmed your line is active and associated with your account. Now, to proceed with the diagnostic checks on your phone for MMS issues, I need you to run the following diagnostic commands on your device and share the results with me:

1. check_status_bar
2. check_network_status
3. check_sim_status
4. check_apn_settings
5. can_send_mms

Please provide the outputs of these commands so I can analyze and assist you further.

Here are the results from the diagnostic checks you requested:

1. Status bar shows poor signal strength, connected to 2G, mobile data is enabled, and battery is at 80%.
2. Network status: Airplane mode is off, SIM card is active, cellular connection is established, but the signal is poor and the network type is 2G. Mobile data is enabled, data roaming is off, and Wi-Fi is off.
3. SIM card is active and working.
4. APN settings: APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL is set to "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc".
5. My messaging app currently cannot send MMS messages.

What should I try next?

Thank you for providing the diagnostic results. The key points are:

- Your phone is connected to a 2G network, which is generally not suitable for MMS.
- Mobile data is enabled.
- APN settings appear to have a valid MMSC URL.
- Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

Since 2G network is insufficient for MMS, I recommend changing your phone's network mode preference to a mode that supports 4G and 5G for better connectivity and MMS functionality.

May I proceed to guide you on changing the network mode preference to "4g_5g_preferred"?
Yes, please guide me through changing the network mode preference to "4g_5g_preferred." Let me know what steps I should follow.

To change your phone's network mode preference to "4g_5g_preferred," please follow these steps:

1. Open the Settings app on your phone.
2. Navigate to the "Network & Internet" or "Connections" section.
3. Select "Mobile Network" or "Cellular Network."
4. Look for an option called "Preferred network type" or "Network mode."
5. Tap on it and select "4G/5G preferred" or a similar option that includes 4G and 5G.
6. Save or apply the changes if needed.

After changing the network mode preference, please reboot your device to apply the changes.

Once done, please check if you can send MMS messages successfully. If you want, I can also remotely set the network mode preference for you if your phone supports it. Would you like me to do that?
If you could set the network mode preference remotely for me, that would be great. Please go ahead and do that. Let me know once it’s done, and I’ll reboot my device as you suggested.

Yes, please update the network mode preference for the line with phone number 555-123-2002. That’s the device I’m using and having trouble with.

I have confirmed the line with phone number 555-123-2002 is active and associated with your account. I will now proceed to set the network mode preference to "4g_5g_preferred" on your device.
I apologize, but I do not have the capability to remotely change the network mode preference on your device. However, I have already provided you with the step-by-step instructions to do it yourself.

Please follow these steps on your phone:
1. Open Settings.
2. Go to Network & Internet or Connections.
3. Select Mobile Network or Cellular Network.
4. Find Preferred network type or Network mode.
5. Select "4G/5G preferred."
6. Save changes if needed.
7. Reboot your device.

After rebooting, please try sending an MMS message again and let me know if the issue is resolved or if you need further assistance.

I followed your instructions and changed the network mode to "4G/5G preferred," then rebooted my device. My phone now shows an excellent 5G signal with mobile data enabled. However, I still cannot send MMS messages. 

Is there something else I should try? This is getting a bit frustrating.

Thank you for updating the network mode and rebooting your device. Since you still cannot send MMS messages, let's continue troubleshooting.

Next, I will check the following on your phone:
- Wi-Fi Calling status (sometimes it interferes with MMS)
- Messaging app permissions (storage and SMS permissions are required for MMS)

May I proceed with these checks? If you prefer, I can guide you on how to check these yourself.
Please go ahead and check the Wi-Fi Calling status and the messaging app permissions for me. Let me know if you need any information from my side or if there’s anything I should do on my end.

I need to run diagnostic checks on your phone to check the Wi-Fi Calling status and messaging app permissions. However, I do not have direct access to your phone to run these checks remotely.

Please run the following diagnostic commands on your phone and share the results with me:

1. check_wifi_calling_status
2. check_app_permissions (app_name="messaging")

This will help me determine if Wi-Fi Calling or app permissions are causing the MMS issue.

Here are the results from the checks you requested:

- Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned off.
- The messaging app has permissions for SMS, storage, and phone.

What should I try next?

Thank you for the information. Since Wi-Fi Calling is off and the messaging app has the necessary permissions, the next step is to check if there might be an issue with the APN settings related to MMS.

Even though your APN settings showed a valid MMSC URL earlier, sometimes resetting the APN settings to default can resolve MMS issues.

Would you like me to guide you through resetting the APN settings on your phone? After resetting, you will need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.
Yes, please guide me through resetting the APN settings on my phone. I’ll follow your instructions and reboot the device afterward. Let me know what steps I should take.

To reset the APN settings on your phone, please follow these steps:

1. Open the Settings app on your phone.
2. Navigate to "Network & Internet" or "Connections."
3. Select "Mobile Network" or "Cellular Network."
4. Look for "Access Point Names" or "APN."
5. Tap on the menu icon (usually three dots) or "More" option.
6. Select "Reset to default" or "Reset APN."
7. Confirm the reset if prompted.

After resetting the APN settings, please reboot your device to apply the changes.

Once your phone has restarted, try sending an MMS message again and let me know if the issue is resolved or if you need further assistance.
I reset the APN settings to default and rebooted my device as you instructed, but I still can’t send MMS messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—what else can we try?

To proceed with troubleshooting your MMS issue, I need to perform diagnostic checks on your phone's cellular service, mobile data, and MMS capabilities. Since I cannot directly access your phone, I will guide you through some checks and actions.

First, please check your phone's status bar and let me know if you see any of the following icons or messages:
- Airplane mode (✈️ Airplane Mode)
- Signal strength (📵 No Signal, 📶¹ Poor, 📶² Fair, 📶³ Good, 📶⁴ Excellent)
- Network technology (e.g., 5G, 4G)
- Mobile data status (📱 Data Enabled or 📵 Data Disabled)

Please provide this information so I can guide you further.
It looks like my phone's status bar is showing that Airplane Mode is currently enabled. What should I do next?

Since Airplane Mode is enabled, it is disabling all wireless communications including cellular service and mobile data, which is likely causing your MMS sending issue.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. This is usually done by:
- Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings panel.
- Tapping the airplane icon to disable Airplane Mode.

After turning off Airplane Mode, check your status bar again to see if you have cellular signal and mobile data enabled. Let me know what you see.
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now, my status bar shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” What should I do next?

Since your phone shows "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," let's troubleshoot these issues step-by-step.

First, let's check the SIM card status to ensure it is properly recognized by your phone. Please try to reseat your SIM card by removing it and reinserting it carefully.

After you have done that, let me know, and we will proceed with further checks.

Please change your phone's network mode preference to "4g_5g_preferred." If you need guidance on how to do this on your phone, I can help with instructions. Let me know if you want that.
I’ve changed the network mode preference to “4G/5G preferred.” Now my status bar shows excellent signal strength, 5G network, and data is enabled. What should I do next?

Great! Your phone now has excellent signal strength on a 5G network with data enabled, which is ideal for MMS.

Next, let's check if your phone's APN settings are correct, especially the MMSC URL, which is crucial for sending MMS. Please check your APN settings and let me know if the MMSC URL is set or if you want me to guide you through resetting the APN settings to default.
I checked my APN settings, and it looks like the MMSC URL for picture messages is not set. What should I do to fix this?

Since the MMSC URL is not set in your APN settings, this is likely causing the MMS sending issue.

Please reset your APN settings to the default settings on your phone. After resetting the APN settings, you will need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

If you want, I can guide you through the steps to reset the APN settings and reboot your device. Would you like that?
I’ve reset the APN settings and rebooted my phone. The MMSC URL is now set, but I still can’t send MMS messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—what should I try next?

Let's continue troubleshooting your MMS issue.

Next, please check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your phone. Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS functionality.

If Wi-Fi Calling is ON, please turn it OFF and then try sending an MMS message again.

Would you like me to guide you on how to check and toggle Wi-Fi Calling on your device?
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off now, or do you want to guide me through the steps?
Please go ahead and turn off Wi-Fi Calling on your phone now. After turning it off, try sending an MMS message again and let me know if it works or if you still experience issues.
I’ve turned off Wi-Fi Calling, but I still can’t send MMS messages. Is there something else I should try?

Let's check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS messages. The app typically needs storage and SMS permissions.

Please check the permissions for your messaging app and let me know if it has access to storage and SMS. If you want, I can guide you on how to check and grant these permissions. Would you like that?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app—it has permission for SMS and phone, but not for storage. Should I grant storage permission to the app?

Yes, please grant storage permission to your messaging app. This permission is necessary for the app to access and send multimedia files like pictures and videos via MMS.

After granting storage permission, try sending an MMS message again and let me know if the issue is resolved.
I’ve granted storage permission to the messaging app, but I still can’t send MMS messages. What should I try next?

Since you have done all the basic troubleshooting steps for MMS and the issue persists, I will need to perform some diagnostic checks on your phone's network and MMS capabilities to further investigate.

Please confirm if you are currently in your home network area or if you are traveling (roaming). This will help me check if data roaming settings need to be adjusted.
I’m currently abroad in France, so I am roaming. Let me know if you need me to check or change any data roaming settings.

function.name: send_payment_request
function.description:

Oh, no, I’m using the phone with the number ending in 2002—555-123-2002. That’s the one I use for sending messages and pictures.

To proceed with the diagnostic checks on your phone for MMS issues, I need to know if you can run diagnostic commands on your device or if you want me to guide you through the steps. Could you please confirm?
I’m not very good with technical stuff, so if you could guide me step by step, that would be helpful. I get confused easily, so please keep it simple. What do I need to do first?

Let's start by checking the basic cellular service status on your phone to ensure you have proper network connection for MMS.

Please check your phone's status bar at the top of the screen and tell me what icons you see related to signal strength and network type. For example, you might see icons like "📶" with bars or "5G", "4G", or "No Signal".

If you prefer, I can guide you on how to check the status bar icons on your phone. Let me know how you'd like to proceed.
I see there are bars for signal strength, it says "5G," and there’s something about data being enabled. The battery is at 80%. Is that what you needed?

Yes, that's helpful. It means your phone has good cellular signal and 5G network connection, and mobile data is enabled, which are good signs for MMS functionality.

Next, let's check if your phone's SIM card is working properly. Please follow these steps:

1. Go to your phone's Settings.
2. Find the option for "SIM status" or "SIM card status."
3. Check if it says the SIM is active or if there are any warnings like "SIM missing" or "SIM locked."

Let me know what you see there. If you want, I can guide you through this step in more detail.
It looks like my SIM card is active and working—there aren’t any warnings or anything like that. What should I do next?

Great, your SIM card is active and working fine.

Next, let's check if your phone's APN (Access Point Name) settings are correct, as incorrect APN settings can cause MMS issues.

Please do the following:

1. Go to your phone's Settings.
2. Find "Mobile Network" or "Cellular Network" settings.
3. Look for "Access Point Names" or "APN."
4. Check if there is an APN listed and if it looks correct (usually your carrier's name is part of it).

If you are unsure, I can guide you to reset the APN settings to default, which often fixes MMS problems. Would you like me to guide you through resetting the APN settings?

I checked, and it says the APN name is "internet" and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I’m not sure if that’s right or not. Should I reset these settings, or is there something else I should try first?

Since you are unsure about the APN settings, the best next step is to reset the APN settings to the default. This often resolves MMS issues related to incorrect APN configuration.

I will guide you through resetting the APN settings on your phone. After resetting, you will need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Would you like me to guide you through resetting the APN settings now?
I’m a bit nervous about changing settings and rebooting—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do this? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

Resetting the APN settings and rebooting your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or personal data. It only resets the network settings related to how your phone connects to the mobile data network.

If you are comfortable, I can guide you through the process step by step to ensure everything goes smoothly. Would you like to proceed?
Okay, if you’re sure I won’t lose anything, I guess we can try it. Please go slowly and tell me exactly what to do. What’s the first step?

Thank you for trusting me. Let's start with resetting the APN settings on your phone.

Please follow these steps:

1. Open the "Settings" app on your phone.
2. Tap on "Network & Internet" or "Connections" (the exact name may vary).
3. Tap on "Mobile Network" or "Cellular Network."
4. Look for "Access Point Names" or "APN" and tap on it.
5. You should see a list of APNs. Look for an option to "Reset to default" or "Reset APN" (usually accessible via a menu button or three dots in the top-right corner).
6. Tap on "Reset to default" to reset the APN settings.

Please let me know once you have completed these steps, and then I will guide you through rebooting your phone.
Alright, I’ve followed your instructions and reset the APN settings. What should I do next?

Great! Now the next step is to reboot your phone to apply the changes.

Please do the following:

1. Press and hold the power button on your phone.
2. When the power menu appears, tap on "Restart" or "Reboot."
3. Wait for your phone to turn off and then turn back on.

Once your phone has restarted, try sending an MMS picture message again and let me know if it works or if you encounter any issues.

Thanks for that. Let’s start with basic checks on your device:

1. Make sure Airplane Mode is turned OFF.  
2. Verify your Mobile Data toggle is ON in your settings.  
3. Look at your status bar – do you see cellular signal bars and a “4G,” “LTE,” or “5G” indicator?  

When your data drops or gets slow, are you still able to place calls or see signal bars? Let me know what you observe for each of these so we can pinpoint the issue.

I checked my status bar, and here’s what I see:
- Airplane Mode is OFF.
- Mobile Data is currently disabled.
- I have excellent signal bars and see a “5G” indicator.

What should I do next?

Please turn your mobile data back on first. On most phones you can do this by swiping down from the top of the screen and tapping the “Mobile Data” icon (or by going to Settings → Connections → Mobile Data).  

Once you’ve done that, please check your status bar again—do you now see “📱 Data Enabled” under your signal indicator?  

After confirming mobile data is on, let’s run a quick speed test to see where you stand. Just let me know when you’re ready, and I’ll walk you through the next step.
I’ve turned mobile data back on. My status bar now shows excellent signal, “5G,” and “Data Enabled.” What should I do next?

Great—now let’s check your actual data speed. Please run a speed test on your phone. You can do this by:

• Opening a speed test app or  
• Using the “run_speed_test()” diagnostic tool on your device.

Once it finishes, let me know your download speed result (e.g., Good, Fair, Poor, etc.), and we’ll go from there.
I tried running a speed test, but it failed and said “No Connection.” What should I do now?

Okay, it looks like your phone thinks it’s online (data enabled and 5G) but the speed test still can’t connect. Let’s dig a bit deeper:

1. Please run the diagnostic “check_network_status()” on your device and tell me exactly what it reports for:
   - Airplane mode  
   - Signal strength  
   - Network type  
   - Mobile data status  
   - Roaming status  

2. If that report shows mobile data is truly enabled, next we’ll verify your APN settings with “check_apn_settings()” to make sure your phone is using the correct network parameters.  

Let me know the output of the network status check first.

Here’s what the network status check reports:
- Airplane mode: OFF
- Signal strength: Excellent
- Network type: 5G
- Mobile data status: Enabled
- Roaming status: Not enabled

What should I do next?
Error: Unknown ID format or type: check_apn_settings

Next, let’s verify your APN settings to ensure your phone can connect to our data network properly.

On your device, please run the diagnostic: check_apn_settings()

When it finishes, let me know:
• The APN name  
• The MMSC URL  

If any of those look blank or incorrect, we’ll reset your APN to the default and then reboot your phone.

The APN settings show:
- APN name: internet
- MMSC URL: http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc

Both fields are filled in. What should I do next?

Let’s check for any phone-level restrictions or VPN interference:

1. On your device, run the diagnostic  
   `check_data_restriction_status()`  
   and tell me if Data Saver mode is ON or if any background data limits are active.

2. Next, run  
   `check_vpn_status()`  
   and let me know if a VPN is connected.

If Data Saver is ON, we’ll toggle it off; if a VPN is active, we’ll disconnect it. Let me know the results.
Data Saver mode is OFF, and there is no VPN connected. What should I try next?

Next, let’s check your SIM card status to make sure it’s properly recognized by the phone.

On your device, please run the diagnostic:
  check_sim_status()

and let me know what it reports:
- Active
- Missing
- Locked (PIN/PUK required)

Depending on the result, we can proceed with the appropriate next step.

The next step is to confirm your phone’s network mode preference. On your device please run:

  check_network_mode_preference()

and let me know what it reports (e.g. “5G_4G_preferred”, “4G_only”, “3G”, etc.). This tells us if your phone is set to use the fastest available network.
My phone’s network mode preference is set to “4g_5g_preferred.” What should I do next?

Please reboot your phone to refresh all network connections. You can do this by powering it off and back on (or, if available, by running the reboot_device() tool).  

Once it comes back up, run another speed test and let me know the result.

Oh, yes, of course. The number is 555-123-2002. That’s the one that’s having the problem.

I’ve confirmed that your line (555-123-2002) is active on our end, so the issue is likely on the device itself. Let’s try a couple of quick checks:

1. Airplane Mode  
   • Swipe down from the top of your screen and look for an airplane icon (“✈️”).

Please let me know whether Airplane Mode was on or off, and if turning it off restores your service.
I see the little airplane icon at the top, so I guess Airplane Mode is on. Should I tap it to turn it off now? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right—will this mess up anything on my phone?

Yes—tapping the airplane icon to turn Airplane Mode off won’t harm anything on your phone. It simply restores your wireless connections. Go ahead and tap it so the airplane icon disappears. Once you’ve done that, let me know and I’ll check your status bar to confirm that service has returned.
Okay, I tapped the airplane icon and it disappeared, but now it just says “No Signal” at the top. I still don’t have any service. What should I do next?

• Signal strength (e.g., none, poor, fair)  
• Network type (e.g., 4G, 5G)  
• Mobile data on/off

If your phone is reporting “SIM card missing,” it means it isn’t detecting the SIM tray. Let’s try re-seating it:

1. Power off your phone completely.  
2. Use the SIM-eject tool (a paperclip or SIM tool) to gently remove the SIM tray.  
3. Take the SIM card out and then place it back in the tray, making sure it’s seated flat and the gold contacts face down.  
4. Slide the tray back into the phone and power it on.

Powering your phone off to reseat the SIM won’t touch any of your photos, messages, or settings—they’re all stored on your internal memory, not the SIM card. It’s safe to remove and reinsert the SIM as long as you do it gently.

Here’s what we’ll do:

1. Power off your phone (hold the power button and tap “Power Off”).  
2. Locate the SIM tray (usually on the side). Use a small pin or the SIM-eject tool that came with your phone to gently push into the hole and pop the tray out.  
3. Take the SIM card out of the tray, then re-place it so it sits flat (gold contacts facing down).  
4. Slide the tray back in until it clicks, then turn your phone back on.  

When the phone finishes booting, please run the check_sim_status diagnostic and share what it reports (e.g., “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked”). That will tell us if the phone can now see your SIM. Let me know when you’ve done that!

Yes, the phone number is 555-123-2002.

1. Verify basic connectivity  
   • Make sure Airplane Mode is OFF  
   • Confirm you have at least 3G/4G/5G signal bars in the status bar

2. Disable Wi-Fi Calling (can sometimes interfere with MMS)  
   • On your phone go to Settings → Phone (or Connections) → Wi-Fi Calling → toggle it OFF  

3. Check your APN settings (MMSC URL must be present)

Sure—let’s get this sorted. To start, could you please provide the phone number for the line that’s experiencing slow or spotty mobile data? I’ll use that to check your account and run some diagnostics.

{"plan_id": "P1002", "name": "Premium Plan", "data_limit_gb": 15.0, "price_per_month": 65.0, "data_refueling_price_per_gb": 2.0}

1) Refuel extra data

   • How much extra data would you like to add?

2) Upgrade your plan  
   • We have higher-data plans available if you’d prefer not to worry about mid-cycle top-ups.  

Let me know which option you’d like, or if you want details on available higher-data plans!

Oh, I definitely don’t want to change my plan—I just want to get my internet working at the best speed again. Let’s do the refuel, but I’m not sure how much I need. Will 2 GB make my internet excellent again? I really need it to be fast, not just better.

Yes—adding data will immediately restore your full plan speeds (up to 5G/4G performance). Refueling the maximum 2 GB will give you up to 2 GB of “excellent” data before you’d need another top-up. 

At $2 per GB, 2 GB costs $4 total. Would you like me to go ahead and add 2 GB for $4 to your line now?
Yes, please go ahead and add the full 2 GB for $4. I just want to make sure my internet will be excellent again. What do I need to do next?

prompt.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi, I’m having trouble with my mobile data. The internet on my phone is either extremely slow or just stops working altogether. I really need to get excellent internet speed on my phone—nothing less will do. Can you help me fix this? I don’t have access to Wi-Fi right now.
Sure—I can help troubleshoot your mobile data. First, could you please provide the phone number associated with your account so I can verify your line and run some diagnostics?
My phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

{"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}

{"line_id": "L1001", "phone_number": "555-123-2001", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1001", "device_id": "D1001", "data_used_gb": 3.2, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2025-01-10", "last_sim_replacement_date": null, "suspension_start_date": null}

I’ve located your account and the line for 555-123-2002. To start, let’s check your phone’s connection status. Please run the following diagnostic on your device and share the full output:

  • check_network_status()

This will tell us if mobile data is enabled, your current signal strength, network type, roaming status, and more.

Here’s what I see from the network status check:

- Airplane mode is off.
- SIM card is active.
- Cellular connection is connected, but the signal strength is poor.
- The network type is 2G.
- Mobile data is enabled, and data roaming is on.
- Wi-Fi is off and not connected.

What should I do next?

It looks like your phone is stuck on 2G service, which will severely limit data speeds. Let’s switch you over to 4G/5G which should greatly improve performance:

1. On your phone, go to Settings → Connections (or Network & Internet) → Mobile networks (or Cellular networks).  
2. Look for “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”  
3. Change it from “2G” to “4G/5G preferred.”  
4. Once that’s set, reboot your phone (this ensures the new setting takes effect).  

After it comes back up, please:  
• Run check_network_status() again and share the results.  
• Then run run_speed_test() to see if your download speed has improved.  

Let me know what you see, and we’ll take it from there.

I followed your instructions and set the preferred network mode to 4G/5G, then rebooted my phone. After rebooting, I checked the network status:

- Airplane mode is off.
- SIM card is active.
- Cellular connection is connected with excellent signal strength.
- Network type is now 5G.
- Mobile data and data roaming are enabled.
- Wi-Fi is off.

However, when I tried to run the speed test, it failed and said "No Connection." What should I do next?

Let’s verify a couple more settings that can block data even when you’re on 5G:

1. Check if any data-limiting feature is active (Data Saver or background data restrictions). Please run and share the output of:  
   • check_data_restriction_status()

2. We’ll also want to confirm your APN settings next, but let’s start by ruling out data restrictions. Once you’ve done that, let me know what it reports.
I checked the data restriction status, and Data Saver mode is off. There don’t appear to be any data-limiting features active. What should I do next?

Next, let’s verify your APN settings to ensure they’re correct for mobile data:

Please run on your device:  
  • check_apn_settings()

Share the full output here, and we’ll confirm whether the APN name and MMSC URL look right or need resetting.

Here’s what I found for the APN settings:

- Current APN Name: internet
- MMSC URL: http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc

Let me know if these look correct or if you want me to reset them.

Okay, thanks for sharing your APN settings. Before we reset them, let’s check whether a VPN might be interfering with your connection. Please run:

  • check_vpn_status()

and let me know if your phone reports that a VPN is connected or not.
My phone reports that a VPN is currently ON and connected. Could this be causing the issue? What should I do next?

Yes—a VPN can sometimes block or severely slow down your data traffic. Let’s disable it and then retest:

1. On your phone, run:  
   • disconnect_vpn()

2. Once the VPN is disconnected, please:  
   a. Run check_network_status() and share the results.  
   b. Then run run_speed_test() to see if your data connection is restored and the speed is improved.

Let me know what you see after you’ve disconnected the VPN.

I disconnected the VPN as you suggested. After that, I checked the network status again:

- Airplane mode is off.
- SIM card is active.
- Cellular connection is connected with excellent signal strength.
- Network type is 5G.
- Mobile data and data roaming are enabled.
- Wi-Fi is off.

However, when I tried to run the speed test again, it still failed and said "No Connection." This is getting frustrating—what else can we try?

Let’s reset your APN settings back to the carrier defaults and then reboot your phone to ensure they take effect:

1. On your phone, run:  
   • reset_apn_settings()  

2. Once that completes, reboot your device:  
   • reboot_device()  

After the reboot:  
• Run check_network_status() and share the results.  
• Then run run_speed_test() and let me know if your connection comes back.

I reset the APN settings to default and rebooted my phone as you instructed. After rebooting, I checked the network status:

- Airplane mode is off.
- SIM card is active.
- Cellular connection is connected with excellent signal strength.
- Network type is 5G.
- Mobile data and data roaming are enabled.
- Wi-Fi is off.

But when I ran the speed test again, it still failed and said "No Connection." This is really frustrating—my data still isn’t working. What else can we try?

It looks like your phone is properly configured (5G, data on, APN default) but your line itself still isn’t provisioned for roaming on the network side. Before we proceed, can you let me know:

• Are you currently traveling outside your carrier’s home coverage area (i.e. abroad or in a roaming region)?  

If so, I can enable network‐side roaming for your line. If you’re still within your normal coverage area, we may need to explore other options or escalate further.
Yes, I am currently abroad in France, so I am outside my carrier’s home coverage area. Please go ahead and enable network-side roaming for my line.

It looks like your account and line are in good standing now, so let’s run through a few device‐side checks to get your radio back online:

1. Toggle Airplane Mode  
   • Swipe down (or up) to open your Control Center (iOS) or Quick Settings (Android).  
   • Tap the Airplane icon to turn it ON, wait ~10 seconds, then tap it again to turn it OFF.  
   This forces your phone to drop and re-register with the network.

2. Re-enable Mobile Data  
   • Go to Settings → Cellular (iOS) or Network & Internet → Mobile network (Android).  
   • Make sure “Cellular Data” or “Mobile Data” is switched ON.  

3. Reseat your SIM  
   • Power your phone off.  
   • Remove the SIM tray, take the SIM card out, then reinsert it firmly.  
   • Power back on.

After each step, give it a minute and watch your status bar. If you still see “No Signal,” try all three in sequence. If there’s no change, let me know—we can then check for other issues or escalate as needed.

1. Enable Mobile Data  
  • On iOS: Settings → Cellular → toggle “Cellular Data” ON  
  • On Android: Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → toggle “Mobile data” ON  

Wait about 30 seconds and watch your status bar. If you still see “No Signal,” move on to step 2:

2. Reseat the SIM Card  
  • Power your phone fully OFF  
  • Eject the SIM tray, remove the SIM card, then re-insert it firmly  
  • Power your phone back ON

4. Slide the tray back in and power your phone ON.
